title: KV backend write serialization relies solely on leases, not optimistic locking
answers: How does the KV storage backend prevent concurrent write conflicts?
Why was GetLatestAndPredecessor / optimistic locking removed from the KV backend?
Do I need to re-check resource version after writing in kvStorageBackend.WriteEvent?
body: Symptom: none (proactive cleanup) — dead optimistic-locking code paths existed alongside always-on leases. Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/resource/storage_backend.go kvStorageBackend.WriteEvent had a post-write re-read/compare step (via dataStore.GetLatestAndPredecessor) guarded by `if !leasesActive`, but leases are always acquired (acquireWriteLease is unconditional, no longer 'maybe'), so that branch was unreachable. Fix pattern: removed GetLatestAndPredecessor, confirmExistence, and the post-write version-check block entirely; concurrency safety now comes only from the per-resource lease acquired in acquireWriteLease before any write. Constraints: any future change to WriteEvent must assume a lease is always held for the duration of the write — do not reintroduce 'optimistic' post-write verification, and do not make lease acquisition conditional without re-adding equivalent conflict detection.

search: Write serialization in kvStorageBackend.WriteEvent relies exclusively on per-resource leases acquired unconditionally in acquireWriteLease, not optimistic locking; the post-write version-check branch (GetLatestAndPredecessor, confirmExistence) was removed because it was unreachable when leases are always active. Any change to WriteEvent or acquireWriteLease in pkg/storage/unified/resource/storage_backend.go must preserve the assumption that a lease is held for the entire write duration. Do not reintroduce post-write optimistic verification, conditionally defer lease acquisition, or add version-compare logic without re-implementing equivalent conflict detection in the lease mechanism.
